title: Ablativus Absolutus Introductio
subtitle: Urbe capta, Caesare duce — constructio 'absoluta' de participio et nomine ambo ablativo.
objectives: Formare ablativum absolutum: nomen/pronomen + participium, ambo ablativo
Vertere ablativum absolutum in clausulam temporalem/causalem/concessivam Anglicam
Uti ablativo absoluto sine participio verbi sum (Caesare duce)
Cognoscere regulam: subiectum ablativi absoluti non debet iam apparere in clausula principali

content.intro: 'Ūrbe captā, mīlitēs discessērunt' — hanc cōnstrūctiōnem breviter in lēctiōne dē participiō perfectō vīdistī. Nunc eam plēnē fōrmālizāmus: est ūna ex cōnstrūctiōnibus māximē elegantibus et frequentibus prōsae Latīnae.
content.explanation: Ablātīvus absolūtus (litt. 'ablative loosed/independent') est phrasis GRAMMATICĒ INDEPENDĒNS ā rēsiduā sententiā: nōmen (vel prōnōmen) + participium, AMBŌ in ablātīvō, concordantēs inter sē.

rules.heading: a) Formatio: Nomen + Participium, Ambo Ablativo
rules.body: Urbe captā (nōmen 'urbs' + participium perfectum 'capta', ambō ablātīvō fēminīnō singulārī) — litterāliter 'with the city having been captured'. Caesare vidente ('with Caesar watching' — participium praesēns, āctiō simultānea).

rules.heading: b) Versiones Possibiles
rules.body: Secundum contextum, ablātīvus absolūtus vertī potest variē: temporāliter ('when/after the city was captured'), causāliter ('because the city was captured'), condicionāliter ('if the city is/were captured'), vel concessīvē ('although the city was captured').

rules.heading: c) Sine Participio: Duo Nomina, vel Nomen + Adiectivum
rules.body: Latīna CARET participiō praesentis verbī 'sum' (*'ēns' nōn exsistit) — ergō ubi Anglica dīceret 'Caesar BEING leader', Latīna simpliciter iūxtāpōnit duo nōmina, VEL nōmen + adiectīvum, ambō ablātīvō, sine verbō ūllō: Caesare duce ('with Caesar as leader' / 'while Caesar was leader'), vīvō patre ('while father was alive', litt. 'father [being] alive').

rules.heading: d) Regula: Subiectum Non Iteratur
rules.body: Nōmen ablātīvī absolūtī nōn dēbet iam esse subiectum vel obiectum clausulae prīncipālis — aliōquīn Latīna praeferret participium simplex concordāns (ut in lēctiōne priōre). Ablātīvus absolūtus intrōdūcit ELEMENTUM NOVUM, grammaticē sēparātum.

examples: Urbe capta, milites discesserunt. — The city having been captured, the soldiers left.
Sole oriente, aves canunt. — With the sun rising, the birds sing.
Caesare duce, Romani vicerunt. — With Caesar as leader, the Romans conquered.
His dictis, discessit. — These things having been said, he departed.
Hostibus victis, pax facta est. — The enemies having been defeated, peace was made.

commonMistakes.wrong: Discipulus tentat formare ablativum absolutum cum verbo 'sum' explicito ('Caesare *ente duce').
commonMistakes.right: 'Caesare duce' — sine ullo verbo, quia participium praesens verbi sum non exsistit.
commonMistakes.why: Haec lacuna gramatica Latina obligat constructionem eliptica, cum duobus nominibus/adiectivo ablativo.

commonMistakes.wrong: Nomen ablativi absoluti est idem ac subiectum clausulae principalis (redundantia).
commonMistakes.right: Ablativus absolutus debet introducere elementum grammaticē separatum a subiecto/obiecto principali.
commonMistakes.why: Si idem nomen esset subiectum utriusque, Latina praeferret simplex participium concordans (Gradus IV, lectio de participio perfecto).

options: participium praesens verbi sum non exsistit

items.prompt: Hostibus ___, pax facta est. (having been defeated — victis)

summary: Ablativus absolutus: nomen/pronomen + participium, ambo ablativo, grammaticē independens.
Versiones: temporaliter, causaliter, condicionaliter, vel concessive.
Sine participio verbi sum: duo nomina, vel nomen + adiectivum, ambo ablativo (Caesare duce).
Subiectum ablativi absoluti non debet coincidere cum subiecto/obiecto clausulae principalis.
